title: Why a Professional Business Website Is More Than an Online Brochure
body:
A professional website is no longer simply an online brochure. It is an important part of how an organisation presents its capabilities, builds credibility and communicates with potential clients.

For engineering firms, consultants, service providers and growing businesses, a well-designed website can support both professional reputation and business development.

However, attractive design alone does not guarantee effectiveness.

A successful business website should address several important considerations.

1. Clear Business Identity
Visitors should immediately understand who the organisation is, what services it provides and how it can assist them.

2. Professional Presentation
A consistent design, clear navigation, accurate information and appropriate visual presentation help establish confidence and trust.

3. Mobile Accessibility
Many potential clients access websites through smartphones. A responsive website should remain easy to read, navigate and use across mobile devices, tablets and computers.

4. Effective Client Communication
A website should make it convenient for visitors to request consultations, submit project enquiries and communicate their requirements without unnecessary complications.

5. Security and Reliability
HTTPS, appropriate security practices, dependable hosting and regular maintenance are important for protecting the website and maintaining visitor confidence.

6. Search Engine Visibility
Clear page structure, relevant content, descriptive headings and basic search engine optimisation can help potential clients discover the organisation online.

7. Continuous Improvement
A website should evolve alongside the business. Updated services, technical insights, project information and improved digital features can strengthen its long-term value.

The Commercial Perspective
A website can be visually impressive yet fail to support business objectives if visitors cannot easily understand its services or make an enquiry.

The objective should therefore be to combine professional presentation, technical functionality and practical business requirements.

At KETCO, we believe website development should focus on creating a credible, accessible and useful digital presence that supports an organisation's professional identity and long-term growth.

A successful website is not merely something people visit. It is a platform that helps businesses communicate, build trust and develop opportunities.

title: Choosing a Site for a Solar Project: More Than Solar Irradiation
body:
High solar irradiation is attractive, but it is only one part of site selection.

A suitable solar site should also be assessed for land availability and cost, flooding and drainage, soil and foundation conditions, road access, proximity to the grid, evacuation requirements, environmental and planning constraints, security, construction logistics and future expansion.

Grid connection can be particularly important. A site with excellent sunlight may become less attractive if major transmission or substation works are required.

For this reason, site screening should compare several candidate locations using a consistent set of technical and commercial criteria. The objective is not simply to find the sunniest site; it is to identify a site that supports a reliable and financially workable project.

title: What Should Be Assessed Before Investing in a Solar PV Project?
body:
Solar PV investment should begin with assessment, not equipment selection.

A preliminary review should examine the available site or rooftop, solar resource, shading, structural or ground conditions, existing electrical infrastructure, transformer and grid capacity, load profile, access, equipment options and expected annual generation.

Commercial factors are equally important. Capital cost, operating cost, financing assumptions, electricity savings or tariff, maintenance requirements and project life all influence viability.

A project can be technically possible but commercially weak. Conversely, a carefully selected and properly structured project can create long-term value.

KETCO’s approach is to consider technical and commercial factors together so that early decisions are based on realistic project conditions rather than isolated assumptions.
